To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) there is significant variation in managerial best practice across countries; (ii) this is associated with significant differences in firm performance; (iii) there is a long tail of poorly managed firms; and (iv) this is due to both low product market competition, and the practice of family firms passing control down to the oldest son (primo genitura).
